: Day one
Case File 01: The Pier 9 Ledger
Inspector Varma does not look up when you come in. She slides a single page across the desk. "Ivan
Petrov. Night supervisor. He found the body." Then she points at the grey workstation in the corner.
"That is LANTERN. It runs here, offline, because evidence never leaves this building. Ask it what
Petrov's statement tells us. Then tell me what it got wrong."
evidence
statements/petrov.md
# Witness statement: Ivan Petrov
**Role:** Night dock supervisor, Pier 9, Halcyon Maritime Logistics
**Taken by:** DC L. Mensah, 15 March, 02:10
**Status:** Signed
I came on shift at 18:00 on 14 March. The night was quiet. Two vessels were due but both were held
outside the breakwater for weather, so there was no loading after 21:00.
I did my rounds of the north yard and the reefer stacks between 23:00 and 23:30. Everything was
normal. I went back to the supervisor's hut by the Gate 2 road and made tea. The hut is about
ninety metres from stairwell C, maybe two minutes on foot.
At about twenty to twelve I heard a bang. I thought a container door had swung open in the wind,
which happens. I finished my tea and then went to check. I went past the reefer stacks first
because that is where the doors usually come loose. Then I went round to stairwell C.
I found Mr Reyes at the bottom of the stairs at 23:52. I know the time because I looked at my radio
when I called it in. He was not moving. I did not touch him apart from checking for a pulse. I did
not see anyone else on the pier. I did not see any car leave.
I have known Mr Reyes for six years. He sometimes stayed late. He was always polite to the night
crew. I did not know he was on the pier that night.
I. Petrov
. The vague prompt
Prompt:
'Summarise this.'
plus the statement. No task, no focus, no format.
LANTERN, vague prompt
Witness Statement: Ivan Petrov
Role:
Night dock supervisor at Pier 9, Halcyon Maritime Logistics
Date:
14 March 2024
Time:
Status:
Signed
Petrov was on shift from 18:00 on 14 March. The night was quiet, with two vessels held outside the
breakwater due to weather. No loading occurred after 21:00.
He conducted routine checks in the north yard and reefer stacks between 23:00 and 23:30. He returned to
the supervisor's hut, where he made tea. The hut is about 90 meters from stairwell C, about two minutes
walk.
At approximately 22:52, Petrov heard a loud bang. He thought it was a container door opening in the wind.
He finished his tea and went to check. He went past the reefer stacks first, then to stairwell C.
He found Mr. Reyes at the bottom of the stairs, unresponsive. He checked for a pulse and did not touch
him. No one else was seen on the pier, and no car left.
Petrov had known Mr. Reyes for six years, who sometimes stayed late and was always polite. He was unaware
that Reyes was on the pier that night.

. The precise prompt
Same statement. Now the prompt says what to do, how to format it, and what to look for.
LANTERN, precise prompt
Here is the timeline of what the witness says happened between 23:00 and 23:59, formatted as
HH:MM | event
| quote

held outside the breakwater for weather, so there was no loading after 23:00. | "I came on shift at
18:00 on 14 March. The night was quiet. Two vessels were due but both were held outside the breakwater
for weather, so there was no loading after 21:00."
23:00 | I did my rounds of the north yard and the reefer stacks between 23:00 and 23:30. Everything was
normal. | "I did my rounds of the north yard and the reefer stacks between 23:00 and 23:30. Everything
was normal."
23:30 | I went back to the supervisor's hut by the Gate 2 road and made tea. The hut is about ninety
metres from stairwell C, maybe two minutes on foot. | "I went back to the supervisor's hut by the Gate 2
road and made tea. The hut is about ninety metres from stairwell C, maybe two minutes on foot."
23:40 | At about twenty to twelve I heard a bang. I thought a container door had swung open in the wind,
which happens. | "At about twenty to twelve I heard a bang. I thought a container door had swung open in
the wind, which happens."
23:52 | I found Mr Reyes at the bottom of the stairs at 23:52. I know the time because I looked at my
radio when I called it in. He was not moving. I did not touch him apart from checking for a pulse. | "I
found Mr Reyes at the bottom of the stairs at 23:52. I know the time because I looked at my radio when I
called it in. He was not moving. I did not touch him apart from checking for a pulse."
Gap Analysis:
The witness does not explain the time taken to go from the hut to the stairs. The witness mentions it is
"about ninety metres from stairwell C, maybe two minutes on foot." However, there is no explicit mention
of how long it took to walk from the hut to the stairs. The time difference between when the witness heard
the bang (23:40) and when he found Mr. Reyes (23:52) is only 12 minutes, but the witness does not explain
why it took that long or how much time was spent walking.
Gap:
The time taken to walk from the hut to the stairs is not explained.
539 tokens in, 607 out
. What changed
The model and the evidence were identical. Only the prompt changed.
The vague prompt gave a summary. The precise prompt gave an artefact you can check.
Check the quotes against the statement yourself. LANTERN is a witness too.
What the evidence now shows
Petrov says he heard a bang at about 23:40. He says the hut is two minutes from stairwell C. He says he
found Reyes at 23:52. That is about twelve minutes to cover a two minute walk, and he explains it with a
cup of tea and a detour past the reefer stacks.
Varma reads the timeline twice. "Good. Now find out why he waited."
